title: IA regulations: registration, qualification and fees
objectives: Explain the two fee modes and caps.
body_md:
Under the **SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013**:

## Registration

- Individuals need the prescribed **qualification** and **NISM certification** (X-A and X-B in the current structure), and relevant experience.
- Non-individuals must meet **net worth** norms and have qualified principal officers.
- IAs must be **fit and proper**, have the infrastructure to maintain records, and renew certification before it lapses.

## Fees

| Mode | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Fixed fee** | Flat annual amount, subject to a cap per family |
| **Assets under advice (AUA)** | Percentage of assets advised on, subject to a cap |

- Fees are charged **in advance for up to a limited period** and refunded pro rata if the agreement ends early.
- Fees are paid by cheque or electronic modes, **not in cash**.
- Fee caps are revised periodically: **verify current limits**.

## Continuing duties

Maintain records for at least **five years**, undergo periodic audit, and maintain a **client agreement**, **risk profile** and **rationale** for each piece of advice.

> **Exam tip:** Fee is from the client only, never from products.
example: An IA charges 1% of the ₹40 lakh assets advised on. That is the AUA mode. If the agreement ends after six months of a one-year fee, the unused part is refunded.
say: My fee is fixed in advance and written in the agreement.
If we end early, the unused fee is returned.
never: I will take a cash fee, no receipt needed.
I also earn commission from the funds I recommend.

check.q: Which fee modes are available to an IA?
check.why: Fixed fee or a percentage of assets under advice, both within caps.

check.q: An IA should keep records for at least:
check.why: Five years is the minimum record retention.
Fees come from the client through traceable modes.
